questions.q: In a hypothetical case, Earth’s mass becomes four times its present value while its diameter becomes half. For the same object at the new surface, how many times would its weight become?
questions.explanation: Weight at the surface is proportional to GM/R^2 for a fixed object mass. The new mass is 4M and halving the diameter also halves the radius, so R becomes R/2. Therefore the new gravitational field is 4 divided by (1/2)^2 = 16 times the original, and the weight also becomes 16 times.

questions.q: A person can lift a maximum mass of 15 kg on Earth. If the same maximum lifting force is used on the Moon, where weight is about one-sixth of that on Earth, what maximum mass can be lifted?
questions.explanation: The person’s maximum force equals the weight of 15 kg on Earth. On the Moon, each kilogram weighs only one-sixth as much. Therefore the same force can balance six times the mass, giving 15 x 6 = 90 kg.

questions.q: The gravitational force between two bodies is F. If both masses are doubled while the separation is unchanged, what is the new force?
questions.explanation: Universal gravitation gives force proportional to the product of the two masses when distance is unchanged. Doubling each mass multiplies the product by 2 x 2 = 4. Hence the new force is 4F.

questions.q: Identical packets are dropped from equal heights above the equator and the north pole under otherwise identical conditions. Which packet reaches Earth first, and why?
options: A) The equatorial packet, because g is greatest at the equator.
B) They arrive together because mass is identical.
C) They arrive together because G is a universal constant.
D) The polar packet, because acceleration due to gravity is greater at the pole than at the equator.
questions.answer: D) The polar packet, because acceleration due to gravity is greater at the pole than at the equator.
questions.explanation: The source states that acceleration due to gravity is least at the equator. For the same drop height, a larger downward acceleration produces a shorter fall time. Therefore the packet dropped above the north pole reaches the surface first.
